items.markdown:
Section 508 is a federal law under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 794d) that requires U.S. federal agencies to make all Information and Communication Technology (ICT) accessible to people with disabilities.[[1]](https://dodcio.defense.gov/508/)

### Key Requirements

- **Equal Access:** Federal employees and members of the public with disabilities must have access to data and digital services comparable to those without disabilities.[[1]](https://dodcio.defense.gov/508/)
- **Covered Technology:** Applies to websites, software applications, electronic documents (PDFs, Word, Excel), hardware, telecommunications, and multimedia.[[1]](https://www.epa.gov/accessibility/learn-about-section-508-and-digital-accessibility)
- **Vendor Impact:** Companies and third-party contractors that build, maintain, or sell technology products to the federal government must also meet Section 508 standards.[[1]](https://www.wcag.com/compliance/section-508/)[[2]](https://www.continualengine.com/blog/section-508-compliance/)
- **Technical Standard:** Compliance is measured by aligning digital systems with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) (specifically WCAG 2.0 Level AA).[[1]](https://www.wcag.com/compliance/section-508/)
- **Management & Resources:** Government-wide guidance, tools, and acquisition help are managed through [Section508.gov](https://www.section508.gov/) and the General Services Administration (GSA).[[1]](https://www.section508.gov/)[[2]](https://www.gsa.gov/policy-regulations/policy/information-technology-policy/it-accessibilitysection-508)
